L2: ### The Holy Roman Empire
L3: The Holy Roman Empire denotes the western empire which encompassed large tracts of Central and Western Europe as well as northern Italy, although the borders changed over time. Brought into being in 800, when Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor in Rome, it was intended to represent the re-establishment of the Western Roman Empire of classical antiquity.
L4: Although the title of emperor of the Holy Roman Empire was not hereditary and the emperor was elected to office, the Habsburgs succeeded in retaining the title for the dynasty from the fifteenth century to the end of the empire in 1806 with very few exceptions.

L1553@P70: administered on behalf of the King by the judges of the Judiciary. It is important to
L1554@P70: note the principle of jurisdictional unity, as justice is administered by a single body of

L1574@P71: Ceuta and Melilla, with the consequent redistribution of political and administrative
L1575@P71: power between central and autonomous authorities. The outcome of this redistribution
L1576@P71: has made Spain one of the most decentralised countries in Europe.
